Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials

on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be

  7
 continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

  ANALYSIS:  As part of the City's  budget  reduction  efforts,  the Public  Works  Department's
  Engineering  Division  implemented  a new organizational  sttucture  during  the last fiscal  year to
  reduce  General  Fund  expenditures.  The restructuring  included  the elimination  of higher-levei
  engineering  classifications  and the redistribution  of responsibilities  among  remaining  staff, As a
  tesult,  the Division  continues  to rely  on specialized  consultant  services  to supplement  internal
  resources  and provide  expettise  in technical  areas, such as traffic  engineering,  that are no longer
  fully  supported  by in-house  staffing.

  1

  10
 W.G.  Zirnmerman  Engineering  (Zimmerman)  has provided  these specialized  traffic  engineering
services  and has been instrumental  in supporting  daily  operations.  Their  services  include  review
of Capital  Improvement  Program  (CIP)  projects,  development  and encroachment  permit  plan
checks,  traffic-related  service  requests,  and  other  specialized  engineering  assignments.  This
support  allows  City  staff  to  maintain  timely  project  delivery  and  permit  processing  while
focusing  on other engineering  priorities.

The  Engineering  Division  currently  requires  approximately  20 hours  per  week  of  consultant
traffic  engineering  support  to meet operational  demands  and maintain  service  levels.

Zimmerman's  current  contract  is scheduled  to expire  on August  8, 2026.  Staff  recommends
approving  Amendment  No.  2 to  Contract  No.  2023-111-CC  to extend  the  contract  for  one
additional  year, through  August  8, 2027, to ensure the continued  availability  of specialized  traffic
engineering  services  and uninternupted  support  for the Division's  operations.

BACKGROUND:  To  supplement  the  Engineering  Division's  in-house  traffic  engineering
capabilities,  the  City  contracts  with  a qualified  traffic  engineering  consultant  to  provide
specialized  engineering  services  on an as-needed  basis.  These  services  support  the review  of
Capital  Improvement  Program  (CIP)  projects,  development  and  encroachment  permit  plan
checks,  traffic-related  service  requests,  and other specialized  engineering  assignments.

On  August  8,  2023,  the  City  Council  approved  Contract  No.  2023-111-CC  with  W.G.
Zirnmerman  Engineering,  Inc.  in the amount  of $340,000  for a two-year  term  ending  August  8,
2025.  On November  25,  2025,  the  City  Council  approved  Amendment  No.  1 to extend  the
contract  for an additional  12 months,  on an as-needed  hourly  basis,  in the amount  of $170,000,
establishing  a new expiration  date of August  8, 2026.

Amendment  No.  2 to Contract  No.  2023-111-CC  will  extend  the contract  for an additional  12
months,  through  August  8, 2027,  in the amount  of $170,000,  allowing  the consultant  to continue
providing  specialized  traffic  engineering  services  on an as-needed  basis.

W.G.  Zirnmerman  Engineering,  Inc. has successfully  provided  traffic  engineering  support  to the
City  for the past three years.  The original  contract  was awarded  through  a competitive  selection
process  in which  W.G.  Zimmerman  Engineering,  Inc. received  the highest  overall  ranking  based
on the City's  established  evaluation  criteria.

 BACKGROUND:  The  Patricia  G. Mitchell  Swim  Stadium,  constructed  in 1976,  included  an
outdated  and non-operational  scoreboard  and  swim  timing  system.  The  existing  equipment  was
unable  to display  event  scores  or lap times,  requiring  the City  to rent timing  equipment  for  swim
meets.  In addition,  the non-operational  scoreboard  had remained  inplace  and unused  for more  than
five  years.

On February  10, 2026,  the City  Council  approved  Contract  No.  2026-14-CC  with  Tricore  in the
amount  of $159,548  for the Patricia G. Mitchell  Swim  Stadium  Scoreboard Project. The Project
replaced  the  obsolete,  non-operational  scoreboard,  swim  timing  system,  touchpad  sensors,  and
associated  wiring,  and integrated  the new  timing  system  with  the Swim  Stadium's  existing  audio
system.  These  improvements  provide  accurate  event  scoring  and  timing  while  enhancing  the
overall  experience  for  participants  and  spectators  during  swim  competitions  and  other  aquatic
events.

Construction  of the Project  was completed  on June 30, 2026.  The contractor  successfully  fulfilled
all  contractual  obligations  and  completed  the  work  in accordance  with  the  approved  plans  and
specifications.  Final  inspections  confirmed  that the improvements  were  constructed  in compliance
with  the contract  requirements  and met the City's  quality  standards.

The  City  Council  may  now  accept  the Project  as complete  and authorize  the City  Clerk  to file  the
Notice  of Completion  with  the Los Angeles  County  Registrar-Recorder/County  Clerk.

 ANALYSIS:  Public  Contract  Code  Section  7107  requires  the  City  to accept  completion  of
construction  and issue public  notice  of such completion  prior  to releasing  the retention  payment.
Filing  the Notice  of Completion  provides  public  notice  that the work  has been completed  and
begins  the 35-day  period  during  which  subcontractors,  suppliers,  and other interested  parties  may
exercise  any lien  rights  associated  with  the Project.  The  City  may  use a portion  or all of the
retention  payment  to satisfy  any valid  stop notices,  liens,  or claims  filed  against  the Project.  If no
such  claims  are filed  within  the statutory  period,  the City  may  release  the retention  and any
remaining  amounts  due to the Contractor.

BACKGROUND:  The  City's  5-Year  Capital  Improvement  Program  (CIP)  is a long-range
planning  and budgeting  document  that identifies  and prioritizes  major  infrastructure  investments
needed  to maintain  and improve  public  facilities.  As part of the CIP, the City  annually  funds  the
Citywide  Residential  Resurfacing  Project  and the Citywide  Sidewalk  Improvement  Project  to
rehabilitate  residential  streets  and repair  or replace  deteriorated  sidewalks,  curbs,  curb  ramps,
and  related  pedestrian  infrastructure.  These  ongoing  programs  help  preserve  the  City's
transportation  network,  improve  public  safety  and accessibility,  extend  the useful  life  of public
infrastructure,  and reduce  long-term  maintenance  costs through  timely  rehabilitation.

On May 13, 2025,  the City  Council  approved  Contract  No. 2025-30-CC  with  Sequel  Contractors,
Inc.  in the amount  of $3,638,773 for the construction  of Phase  IV  of the RRP  Project.  This
project  entailed  rehabilitating  11 street  segments  located  throughout  the City.  Work  included
fixing  street pavements,  sidewalks,  and ADA  improvements.  Construction  began  on March  20,
2025,  and was completed  on July 20, 2026.

A  total  of  five  change  orders  were  needed  to  complete  construction,  increasing  the  total
construction  contract  amount  to $4,821,916.  Below  is a summary  of the change  orders.

  *  Change  Order  No.  1, in the  amount  of  $194,322,  entailed  upgrading  the  planned
  improvements  on Pinehurst  Avenue,  Hildreth  Avenue,  and Industrial  Avenue  from  cape
  seal to cold milling  and rubberized  asphalt  hot-mix  overlay,  including  localized  pavement
  and concrete  repairs  and additional  striping.

  *  Change  Order  No.  2, in the amount  of $339,572,  entailed  adding  and adjusting  work
  needed  to address  field  conditions  on Liberty  Boulevard,  Missouri  Avenue,  Madison
  Avenue,  and  Frontage  Road.  The  work  included  concrete  restoration,  adjustments  to
  pavement  grinding  and asphalt  quantities,  additional  striping,  water. shut-off  valves,  curb
  and  gutter  reconstruction,  roadway  base  work,  and  weekend  water-main  shutdown
  operations.

  *  Change  Order  No.  3, reduced  the contract  amount  by $266,554  due to the reconciliation
  of the original  bid quantities  with  the actual  as-built  quantities,  deducting  work  that was
  not  performed  or  no  longer  required,  and  adjusting  minor  quantity  overnins  and
  undenuns  based on field  verification.

  *  Change  Order  No.  4,  in  the  amount  of  $879,750,  was  needed  to  incorporate
  improvements  on additional  streets  into  the  project  including  Wood  Avenue,  Seville
  Avenue,  Kansas  Avenue,  and East Frontage  Road.

  2  66
   *  Change  Order  No.  5 reconciles  the  final  quantities  of work  performed  and  other  final
  contract  adjustments  required  for project  closeout.  This  change  order  adjusts  the contract
  bid quantities  to reflect  the actual  quantities  constructed  in the field,  adding  $107,971  for
  quantity  increases  and reducing  $71,918  for work  not  required  to complete  construction,

improvements.  The  additional  work  has  now  been  completed;  the  Project  is ready  for  final
acceptance.

  SUBJECT:  ANNUAL  ST ATEMENT  OF  INVESTMENT  POLICY  AND  QUARTERLY
  INVESTMENT  REPORT  FOR  THE  QUARTER  ENDED  JUNE  30, 2026

  PURPOSE:  California  Government  Code  Section  53646  provides  for  the  Director  of
  Administrative  Services,  as tlie City's  chief  fiscal  officer,  to annually  render  a Statement  of
  Investment  Policy  to the City Council  for consideration  at a p'ublic meeting,  and to render a report
  to the City  Council,  the City Manager,  and the internal  auditor  within  45 days following  the end
  of each quarter providing  detailed  information  on all investments  of the City. Both provisions  are
  permissive  under state law, and the Legislature  encourages  local agencies to continue  the practice.
  The City follows  both, and the Statement  of Investment  Policy  presented  here malces both binding
  on staff once adopted.  This Agenda  Bill  presents the annual policy  and the qumterly  report for the
  quarter ended June 30, 2026, for the City Council's  consideration  at a single meeting.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will  consider:
  a.  Adopt  a Resolution  approving  the City's  Annual  Statement  of Investment  Policy  for Fiscal
  Year  2026-27  and delegating  investment  authority  to the Director  of  Administrative
  Services  pursuant  to Government  Code Section  53607 for one year; and

  b.  Receive  and file the Quarterly  Investment  Report for the quarter  ended June 30, 2026.

  SUMMARY:  The City's  investment  program  is governed  by a Statement  of Investment  Policy
  adopted by the City Council,  which  staff and the City's  investment  adviser are required  to follow.
  State investment  law has changed,  and the City  has retained  a discretionary  external  investment
  adviser,  Meeder  Public  Funds,  Inc., to manage  its operating  portfolio.  The policy  presented  as
  Attachment  A is therefore  a comprehensive  update rather than a routine  annual refresh,

  The principal  changes are provisions  governing  the discretionary  investment  adviser,  including
  best execution,  disclosure  of adviser  and affiliate  compensation,  and the adviser's  maintenance  of
  the approved  broker/dealer  list subject to the Director's  review;  an updated  schedule  of authorized
  investments  reflecting  the California  Debt  and Investment  Advisory  Commission  2026 Local
  Agency  Investment  Guidelines;  a stated  performance  benchmark;  a reporting  section;  and
  provisions  reflecting  Senate Bill  827 (2025)  fiscal andfinancial  training  and SenateBill  852 (2025)
  electronic  Form 700 filing.

ANALYSIS:

Annual  Statement  of Investment  Policy

California  Government  Code  Section  53646  provides  for the aru'iual rendering  of a Statement  of
Investment  Policy  to the City  Council  for  consideration  at a public  meeting.  The  Director  of
Administrative  Services  and the City  Manager  review  the policy  annually  and submit  it to the City
Council  for consideration  and approval  at a public  meeting.  The City's  current  investment  policy
has not been comprehensively  updated  since 2004.  The policy  presented  for adoption  applies  to
Fiscal  Year 2026-27.

The proposed  policy  (Attachment  A) remains  conservative.  It authorizes  only  those investments
permitted  under  California  Government  Code Section  53600  et seq., and prioritizes,  in order:  (1)
safety of principal;  (2) liquidity  sufficient  to meet the City's  daily  cash flow  needs; and (3) a market
rate of return.  The policy  requires  diversification  by security  type,  issuer,  industry,  and maturity;
limits  any single corporate  or bank issuer to 10% of the portfolio;  and limits  the maximum  maturity
of any investment  to five  years from  settlement  unless  the City  Council  grants  express  authority
no less than three months  before  purchase.

The most  significant  change  from  the prior  policy  is the express  recognition  of a discretionary
external  investment  adviser.  Under  the proposed  policy,  and under  the  annual  delegation  of
investment  authority  made pursuant  to Government  Code  Section  53607,  Meeder  Public  Funds,
Inc. is authorized  to buy and sell authorized  securities  on the City's  behalf  without  transaction-by-
transaction  approval.  That authority  is bounded  by several  controls.  The adviser  has no custody  of
City  assets. All  trades  settle  on a delivery-versus-payment  basis through  the City's  independent
custodian.  The adviser  must  obtain  and document  best execution.  The adviser  may not place  City
funds  in any product  from  which  it or an affiliate  earns additional  fees without  the Director's  prior
written  approval.  The Director  may  direct  that any broker  or dealer  not be used. The delegation
expires  after one year unless  the City  Council  renews  it.

Quarterly  Investment  Report

California  Government  Code  Section  53646  provides  for a quarterly  report  to the City  Council,
the City  Manager,  and the internal  auditor  within  45 days following  the end of the quarter.  This
report  provides  the City Council  with  a current  snapshot  ofthe  City's  investment  holdings,  liquidity
position,  and compliance  with  applicable  laws  and policies  as of June 30, 2026.  Attached  is the
Investment  Report  for the quarter  ended  June 30, 2026  (Attachment  B), prepared  by the City's
investment  adviser,  Meeder  Public  Funds,  Inc.  Market  values  shown  in the report  are obtained
from  an independent  pricing  source  and  not  from  any  party  to the  underlying  transactions,

  ST ATEMENT  OF INVESTMENT  POLICY

1. POLICY

It is the policy of the City of South Gate ("City") to invest public funds in a prudent manner  that
complies with all applicable state and local laws and that provides, in the following priority order:
first, the safety of principal; second, the liquidity necessary to meet the City's daily cash flow
demands; and third, a market rate of return. This policy conforms to California  Government
Code Sections 53600 et seq. governing the investment of local agency funds.

In accordance  with Government  Code Section 53646, the Director of Administrative  Services
("Director")  will annually  render a Statement  of Investment  Policy to the City Council.  The
Director and the City Manager shall review this policy annually and submit it to the City Council
for consideration and approval at a public meeting.

11. SCOPE

This policy applies to all investment activities and financial assets of the City that are accounted
for in the City's Annual Comprehensive  Financial Report (ACFR), including the following fund
types:

  *  General  Fund
  *  Special  Revenue  Funds
  *  Debt  Service  Funds
  *  Capital  Project  Funds
  *  Enterprise  Funds
  *  Internal  Service  Funds
  *  Trust and Agency Funds
  *  Any new fund created by the City Council, unless specifically  exempted

This policy does not apply to the City's employee  retirement  funds, which are administered
separately,  or to the proceeds of debt issues that are held and invested by trustees under the
applicable  indenture or bond documents.  Bond proceeds shall be invested in accordance  with
the permitted  investment  provisions  of the governing  bond documents  or, where  those
documents  are silent, in accordance  with this policy and Government  Code Section 53601.

 Ill.  PRUDENCE

The standard  of prudence  applied  by the Director  and by all persons  authorized  to make
investment  decisions  on the  City's  behalf  is the  prudent  investor  standard  set forth  in
Government  Code Section  53600.3,  applied  in the context  of managing  the overall  portfolio.
Under that standard,  when investing,  reinvesting,  purchasing,  acquiring,  exchanging,  selling,
and managing  public funds, a trustee  shall act with care, skill, prudence,  and diligence  under
the circumstances  then prevailing,  including,  but not limited to, the general economic  conditions
and the anticipated  needs  of the City, that a prudent  person  acting  in a like capacity  and
familiarity  with those matters would use in the conduct  of funds of a like character  and with like
aims, to safeguard  the principal  and maintain  the liquidity needs of the City.

Persons  authorized  to make  investment  decisions  on behalf  of the City are trustees  and
therefore  fiduciaries  subject  to the prudent  investor  standard.  Investment  officers  and staff
acting in accordance  with this policy and written procedures,  and exercising  due diligence,  shall
be relieved  of personal  responsibility  for an individual  security's  credit  risk or market  price
changes,  provided  that deviations  from expectations  are reported  in a timely manner  and that
appropriate  action is taken to control adverse  developments.

IV.  OBJECTIVES

Consistent  with  Government  Code  Section  53600.5,  the  primary  objectives  of the City's
investment  activities,  in priority order, are safety, liquidity,  and return on investment.

A. Safety.  Safety of principal  is the foremost  objective  of the investment  program.  Investments
shall be undertaken  in a manner  that seeks to preserve  capital in the overall portfolio  through
careful evaluation  of credit risk and market risk.

  1. Credit  risk, the risk of loss due to the failure of the issuer of a security,  shall be mitigated
  by investing  only in high-quality  issuers and by diversifying  the portfolio so that the failure of
  any one issuer would not materially  harm the City's cash flow.

  2.  Market  risk,  the risk of market  value fluctuation  from changes  in the general  level of
  interest rates, shall be mitigated  by limiting the weighted  average  maturity  of the portfolio to
  less than five years and by structuring  maturities  to meet the City's anticipated  cash needs.

B.  Liquidity.  The investment  portfolio  shall remain  sufficiently  liquid to meet all operating
requirements  that may be reasonably  anticipated.  The City will maintain  a laddered  portfolio
with regularly  scheduled  maturities  and will invest primarily  in securities  with active secondary
or resale markets.

C.  Return  on Investment.  The portfolio  shall be designed  to attain a market  rate of return
throughout  budgetary  and economic  cycles,  commensurate  with the risk constraints  in this
policy and the cash flow characteristics  of the portfolio.

 V.  DELEGATION  OF AUTHORITY

The City Council,  consistent  with Government  Code Sections  53601 and 53607,  retains  ultimate
responsibility  for the City's investment  program.  Pursuant  to Government  Code Section  53607,
Chapter  1.08 of the South Gate Municipal  Code,  and City Council  action  of February  25, 1997,
the City Council  delegates  to the Director  of Administrative  Services  the authority  to invest  and
reinvest  City funds  and to sell or exchange  securities.  This delegation  is granted  for a one-year
period  and is renewable  annually  by the City Council.  The Director  assumes  full responsibility
for all transactions  until the delegation  is revoked  or expires  and shall establish  a system  of
internal  controls  to regulate  the activities  of subordinate  staff.  In the absence  of the Director,
the City Manager  shall serve  as administrator  of the investment  program.

The City has retained  a discretionary  external  investment  adviser  (the "Investment  Adviser")
under an agreement  approved  by the City Council  to manage  the City's core operating  portfolio.
As of the effective  date  of this policy,  the Investment  Adviser  is Meeder  Public  Funds,  Inc.
Pursuant  to that agreement  and the annual  delegation  of authority  under  Government  Code
Section  53607,  the Investment  Adviser  is authorized  to buy and sell authorized  securities  on
the City's  behalf  on a discretionary  basis,  in strict compliance  with this policy  and applicable
law. The Investment  Adviser  acts as an agent of the City under the oversight  of the Director  and
has no custody  of City assets.

Consistent  with Government  Code Section  53600.3,  the City retains  its fiduciary  responsibility
for the investment  program  and does not delegate  that responsibility  to the Investment  Adviser.
The Director  remains  responsible  for oversight  of the Investment  Adviser,  for the annual  review
and renewal  of the delegation  of authority,  and for rendering  the City's  investment  reports  and
this policy to the City Council.

Consistent  with Senate  Bill 827 (2025),  local agency  officials  with financial  responsibilities  shall
complete  at least two hours  of fiscal  and financial  training  every  two years,  covering,  among
other topics,  cash management  and investments  and the prudent  investor  standard.

The costs  of administering  the investment  program,  including  custodial,  investment  advisory,
banking,  and auditing  fees,  are budgeted  annually  and apportioned  to the funds  that benefit
from investment  earnings  in a manner  consistent  with the City's accounting  practices.

activity  that could  conflict  with the proper  execution  of the investment  program  or that could
impair  their  ability  to make  impartial  decisions.  The  Director  and all designated  investment
officials  are required  to file annual  Statements  of Economic  Interests  (Form 700) as required  by
the Fair Political  Practices  Commission  (FPPC).  Consistent  with Senate  Bill 852 (2025),  public
officials  who  manage  the City's  public  investments  shall  file Form  700 through  the  FPPC's
electronic  filing system.

Execution  and Adviser  Conflicts
The Investment  Adviser  is responsible  for obtaining  best execution  on all transactions  executed

IX.  REVIEW  OF INVESTMENT  PORTFOLIO
Investments  must  comply  with  Section  Vlll  at the time of purchase.  The  Investment  Adviser
shall monitor  the portfolio  on an ongoing  basis for compliance  with this policy and shall promptly
report  any exception  to the Director.  Because  a security  may cease  to comply  after purchase,
for example  due to a rating downgrade  or a change  in portfolio  composition,  the Director  shall
review  the portfolio  at least annually  to identify  any securities  that no longer  comply  with this
policy. Any investment  held that no longer  meets the guidelines  of this policy shall be reviewed,
the City Council  shall  be advised  of the situation  and the intended  course  of action,  and at
maturity  or liquidation  such funds shall be reinvested  in compliance  with this policy. The Director
shall report  to the City Council,  and to any oversight  body should  one exist,  major  and critical
instances  of noncompliance  identified  through  this review.

X.  INVESTMENT  POOLS  AND  MUTUAL  FUNDS
Before  the City invests  in any pooled  investment  vehicle  or fund,  including  the Local Agency
Investment  Fund (LAIF),  county  pooled  investment  funds,  joint powers  authority  pools,  mutual
funds,  and money  market  mutual  funds,  and on a continuing  basis  thereafter,  the Investment
Adviser,  on behalf  of the City and subject  to the Director's  oversight,  shall conduct  a thorough
investigation  of the pool or fund and will make best efforts  to obtain  the following  information:

  *  A description  of the eligible  investment  securities  and a written  statement  of the pool's
  or fund's  investment  policy  and objectives.
  *  A description  of how interest  is calculated  and distributed  and how gains and losses
  are treated.
  *  A description  of how the securities  are safeguarded,  including  settlement  processes,
  how often the securities  are priced,  and how offen the program  is audited.

XI.  COLLATERALIZATION

Pursuant  to  Government  Code  Sections  53630  et  seq.  and  53651  through  53667,
collateralization  is required on certificates  of deposit and on repurchase  and reverse repurchase
agreements.  Depositories  must secure  public fund deposits  by maintaining  collateral  with a
market value of at least 11 0% of the value of the deposit,  or 1 50% where  mortgage-backed
securities  are used as collateral.  Repurchase  and reverse  repurchase  agreements  shall be
collateralized  at 1 02% of the value of principal and accrued interest, marked to market. A waiver
may apply  to the extent  that  City  funds  are  insured  by the  Federal  Deposit  Insurance
Corporation  (FDIC).

Collateral  shall be held by an independent  third party with which the City has a current custodial
agreement,  and a clearly marked  safekeeping  receipt evidencing  ownership  shall be supplied
to and retained  by the City. The right of collateral  substitution  is granted.  A signed  Master
Repurchase  Agreement  shall be executed  with any counterparty  before the City enters into a
repurchase  or reverse repurchase  agreement.

Xll.  SAFEKEEPING  AND  CUSTODY

Consistent  with Government  Code Section  53608, all security  transactions  entered  into on the
City's behalf, including  collateral  for repurchase  agreements,  shall be conducted  on a delivery-
versus-payment  (DVP) basis, so that securities  are received  before City funds  are released.
The City shall designate  an independent  third-party  custodian  to hold all securities  in the City's
name, evidenced  by safekeeping  receipts.  The Investment  Adviser  shall have no custody  of
City assets and shall direct all transactions  for settlement  on a DVP basis through  the City's
designated  custodian.  The custodian  shall provide the City with a report on at least an annual
basis.

 Xlll.  DIVERSIFICATION

The purpose  of diversification  is to reduce  overall  portfolio  risk while attaining  a market  rate of
return  and to enable  the City to meet its anticipated  cash requirements.  The City will diversify
its investments  by security  type,  issuer,  industry,  and  maturity.  With  the exception  of  u.s.
Treasury  obligations,  u.s. Agency  obligations,  overnight  sweep  accounts,  and  authorized
investment  pools such as LAIF, no more than 10% of the total portfolio  will be invested  in the
securities  of any  single  corporate  or bank  issuer.  The  per-issuer  and  per-category  limits
established  by state law and set forth in Figure 1 and its Table  of Notes  also apply  at the time
of purchase.

XIV.  MAXIMUM  MATURITIES

To the extent  possible,  the City will match  its investments  to anticipated  cash flow requirements.
Unless  matched  to a specific  cash flow, the City will not directly  invest  in securities  maturing
more than five years  from the date of settlement,  unless  the City Council  has granted  express
authority  to do so no less than three  months  prior to purchase,  consistent  with  Government
Code  Section  53601.  Reserve  funds  may be invested  in securities  exceeding  five years  only
where  the maturities  are made to coincide  as nearly as practicable  with the expected  use of the
funds  and the City Council  has granted  express  authority.  Forward  settlement  on new issues
shall not exceed  45 days from the time of investment.

XV.  INTERNAL  CONTROLS
The  Director  is responsible  for establishing  and  maintaining  an internal  control  structure
designed  to ensure  that the assets  of the City are protected  from  loss, theff,  fraud,  or misuse
and to regulate  the activities  of subordinate  staff. The internal  control  structure  shall address
the following:

  *  Control  of collusion.
  *  Separation  of transaction  authority  from accounting  and recordkeeping.
  *  Custodial  safekeeping.
  *  Avoidance  of physical  delivery  of securities.
  *  Clear delegation  of authority  to subordinate  staff.
  *  Written  confirmation  of transactions  for investments  and wire transfers.
  *  Dual authorization  of wire transfers
  *  Development  of a wire transfer  agreement  with the lead bank and third-party  custodian.
The  Director  shall  establish  an annual  process  of independent  review  by the City's  external
auditor.  This review  provides  internal  control  by assuring  compliance  with the City's policies  and
procedures.

The City has engaged  a discretionary  Investment  Adviser  to manage  its core operating  portfolio

City's  risk  constraints  and  cash-flow  needs.  The  portfolio  shall  be managed  relative  to a
benchmark  that reflects  its duration  and risk profile.  Unless  otherwise  mutually  agreed  between
the  City  and  the  Investment  Adviser,  the  benchmark  is the  ICE  BofA  1-3  Year  u.s.
Government/Corporate  Index.  Funds  needed  for near-term  liquidity  may be held in LAIF, other
authorized  investment  pools  such  as CAMP,  or overnight  sweep  vehicles.  The  Investment
Adviser  shall  measure  and  report  portfolio  performance  relative  to the benchmark,  and the
benchmark  may  change  over time  based  on market  conditions,  cash-flow  requirements,  or
agreement  between  the City and the Investment  Adviser.

XVII.  REPORTING

California  Government  Code establishes  two reporting  requirements  applicable  to the City, and
the City will satisfy  both. Under the City's agreement  with its Investment  Adviser,  the Investment
Adviser  prepares  these  reports;  the Director  reviews  them and renders  or presents  them to the
City Council.

Monthly  transaction  report  (Section  53607).  Because  the  City  Council  has  delegated
investment  authority  under  Section  53607,  a monthly  report  of all investment  transactions,
provided  by the Investment  Advisor,  shall be made  available  to the City Council.

Quarterly  investment  report  (Section  53646).  The Investment  Adviser  shall prepare,  and the
Director  shall  render  to the City Council,  the City Manager,  and the internal  auditor  within  45

  *  A description  of any of the City's funds,  investments,  or programs  that are under the
  management  of contracted  parties,  including  lending  programs.

 GLOSSARY
Because this policy is available to the public as well as to the City Council, the following  glossary
defines terms of a technical  nature used in the policy.

Annual  Comprehensive  Financial  Report  (ACFR):  The City's official annual financial  report,
prepared in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles,  including  financial
statements, supporting schedules, and statistical information.
Agencies:  Federal agency securities  and government-sponsored  enterprise  (GSE)
obligations,  including  those of the Federal Home Loan Bank, Federal National  Mortgage
Association, Federal Home Loan Mortgage  Corporation,  Federal  Farm Credit Bank, and
Federal Agricultural Mortgage Corporation.

Bankers' Acceptance  (BA): A draff or bill of exchange  accepted  by a bank or trust company,
in which the accepting  institution guarantees payment.
California  Asset  Management  Program  (CAMP):  A joint powers authority  investment  pool
that provides California public agencies  with a professionally  managed,  short-term  investment
vehicle for surplus funds.

Benchmark:  A comparative  base for measuring  the performance  or risk of the portfolio,
ideally correlated  to the level of risk and the average  duration  of the portfolio's  investments
Bid: The price offered for a security  by a prospective  buyer.
Broker:  A party that brings buyers and sellers together  for a commission  and does not take a
position  in the securities.

Certificate  of Deposit (CD): A time deposit with a specific  maturity  evidenced  by a certificate,
issued in either negotiable or non-negotiable form.

Certificate  of Deposit  Account  Registry  Service  (CDARS):  A private placement  service
that allows a local agency to obtain FDIC insurance on deposits exceeding $250,000 by
distributing them among participating institutions in amounts below the insurance limit.
Collateral: Securities or other property pledged to secure repayment  of a loan, or pledged  by
a bank to secure deposits of public funds.
Coupon:  The stated annual interest  rate a bond issuer pays on the bond's face value.
Dealer:  A party that acts as a principal,  buying and selling securities  for its own account.
Delivery  Versus  Payment  (DVP):  Settlement  in which the exchange  of securities  and the
exchange  of payment  occur simultaneously,  so that funds are not released  until securities  are
received.

Diversification:  Allocating investment funds among a variety of security types, issuers, and
maturities to reduce overall portfolio risk.
Duration: A measure of the sensitivity  of a fixed-income  investment's  price to a change in
interest rates, expressed in years.
Federal  Deposit  Insurance  Corporation  (FDIC): A federal agency that insures bank
deposits,  currently  up to $250,000  per depositor  per insured institution.

 Investment  Adviser:  The SEC-registered  investment  adviser  retained  by the City under a
Council-approved  agreement  to manage  the City's operating  portfolio  on a discretionary  basis,

Liquidity:  The ease with which  an asset can be converted  to cash without  a substantial  loss
of value.

Local  Agency  Investment  Fund  (LAIF):  A voluntary  investment  pool administered  by the
California  State Treasurer  in which  local agencies  may invest surplus  funds.

Market  Value:  The price at which  a security  could presumably  be purchased  or sold at a
given time.

Master  Repurchase  Agreement:  A written  contract  governing  all repurchase  and reverse
repurchase  transactions  between  the parties,  establishing  each party's  rights,  including  the
right to liquidate  collateral  upon default.

Maturity:  The date on which  the principal  or stated value  of an investment  becomes  due and
payable.

Medium-Term  Notes:  Corporate  and depository  institution  debt securities  with a maximum
remaining  maturity  of five years  or less, issued  by entities  organized  and operating  within  the
United  States.

Money  Market:  The market  in which  short-term  debt instruments  such as Treasury  bills,
commercial  paper,  and bankers'  acceptances  are issued  and traded.

Negotiable  Certificate  of Deposit:  A large-denomination  certificate  of deposit  that can be
sold in the secondary  market  prior to maturity.

NRSRO:  A Nationally  Recognized  Statistical  Rating  Organization  registered  with the SEC,
such as Moody's,  S&P Global  Ratings,  or Fitch Ratings.

Portfolio:  The collection  of securities  and investments  held by the City.

Primary  Dealer:  A government  securities  dealer  that reports  market  activity  and positions  to,
and is subject  to the oversight  of, the Federal  Reserve  Bank of New York.

Prudent  Investor  Standard:  The standard  set forth in Government  Code Section  53600.3
requiring  a trustee  to act with care, skill, prudence,  and diligence  in managing  public funds to
safeguard  principal  and maintain  liquidity.

Rate of Return:  The yield obtainable  on a security  based  on its purchase  price or current
market  price.

Repurchase  Agreement  (Repo):  A transaction  in which  the City purchases  securities  from a
counterparty  that agrees  to repurchase  them at a fixed price on a fixed date; in effect  a
collateralized  short-term  investment  of City funds.

Reverse  Repurchase  Agreement  (Reverse  Repo):  A transaction  in which  the City sells
securities  to a counterparty  and agrees  to repurchase  them at a specified  later date and price;
in effect  a form of short-term  borrowing.

 ANALYSIS:  The Measure  A Funding  Agreement  outlines  the terms  and conditions  for the City's
allocation,  including  reporting,  monitoring,  and compliance  requirements.  The City's  approved
Scope of Work  identifies  three primary  initiatives  to be supported  by Measure  A resources.  First,
the City  will  'fund four  interim  shelter  beds at the Salvation  Army  Bell  Shelter.  These  beds will
provide  immediate  housing  options  coupled  with  wraparound  services  to facilitate  transitions  to
permanent  housing.  Second,  interim  housing  in the form  ofmotel  vouchers  will  provide  emergency
temporary  shelter  to individuals  and families  experiencing  homelessness  due to domestic  violence
or other crisis.  Third,  Measure  A 'funds will  provide  time-limited  rental  assistance  programs  (rental
arrears,  emergency  rental  assistance  programs,  move-in  assistance)  for  households  at risk  of
homelessness,  administered  through  our City  Housing  Department.  Additionally,  the agreement
includes  case management  and outreach  services  in the form  of a Housing  Navigator  that will
coordinate  services  and serve individuals  and families  experiencing  homelessness.

BACKGROUND:  On November  5, 2024,  Los Angeles  County  voters  approved  Measure  A, a
new half-cent  sales tax replacing  the expiring  Measure  H one-quarter-cent  tax. While  Measure  H
provided  significant  resources  for homelessness  programs,  funds  were largely  administered  at the
County  level.  Measure  A strengthens  local  government  participation  by dedicating  15 percent  of
annual  revenues  to the Local  Solutions  Fund,  which  is distributed  directly  to cities,  councils  of
governrnent,  and unincorporated  areas. This  direct  allocation  provides  cities  with  flexibility  and
resources  to implement  tailored  strategies  while  still  aligning  with  countywide  goals.

Under  the Local  Solutions  Fund,  the City  will  receive  a direct  allocation  of $495,742  for Fiscal
Year 2025/2026  and $460,078  for Fiscal  Year 2026/2027.  The City executed  a Funding  Agreement
with the County  for Measure  A Local  Solutions  Fund, Contract:  HI-25-024  on December  23, 2025,
with  a performance  period  ending  on June 30, 2031. The direct  allocation  varies  every fiscal  year,
up  to June 30, 2031.
